correctness.rationale: For each code variable \(X_{n,j}\), the support bound \(X_{n,j}\le j\) implies the parking inequalities. At midpoint, surplus is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables with mean \(m_n\) and variance at most \(m_n\). The published Diaconis--Hicks Theorem 15 gives a non-atomic Brownian-excursion marginal for the uniform surplus scaled by \(\sqrt n\). For \(m_n\le n^{2/3}\), Chebyshev concentrates alternative surplus in width \(n^{5/12}=o(\sqrt n)\), whose uniform probability vanishes by anti-concentration. For \(m_n>n^{2/3}\), alternative surplus exceeds half its mean with probability tending to one while remaining far above the tight uniform \(\sqrt n\)-scale. All bounds are uniform over arbitrary row-dependent marginals. Mallows laws have independent inversion coordinates. The finite exact checks do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Pinsky (arXiv:2509.24452v2) explicitly poses the full-law TV-minimum question and proves independent Mallows code and one-coordinate/occupancy limits, not the answer. Diaconis--Hicks Theorem 15 supplies the uniform Brownian-excursion profile but does not compare it with independent-code measures. The new separation argument combines the independent-code Poisson--binomial surplus with the non-atomic uniform excursion limit to rule out all independent factorial-coordinate samplers uniformly. No published equivalent was identified by the recorded comparisons; hidden priority remains possible.

value.rationale: The result resolves the explicit full-law total-variation minimization question in Pinsky (2025) completely: the limiting distance is 1 for every parameter regime, including arbitrary n-dependent parameters. It also identifies the broad structural barrier for *all* independent factorial-code samplers, explaining how low-dimensional marginal agreement can coexist with complete global variation separation. This is a motivated exact asymptotic impossibility theorem about a new family of random parking functions, not an arbitrary finite slice.
